4ceb2dfa69: How it works, without the jargon
5c26d85db5: Think of a public notebook that nobody owns.
5ef17b2ff5: Every bitcoin transaction ever made is written in one ledger. Identical copies are kept by tens of thousands of computers ("nodes") around the world. Anyone can keep a copy.
b24dadf889: A lottery for the next page
6c992b5e0c: Every ~10 minutes, "miners" compete to add the next page (a block) by solving a puzzle that is very hard to solve but instant to check. The winner earns new bitcoin plus fees.
cfa3a10098: Every node independently checks every page against the rules. Try to spend coins twice, or create coins from nothing, and the network simply ignores you. No permission needed, and no exceptions.
f3240e8316: Mining turns real-world energy into security, much like digging gold out of the ground. The cost can't be faked, so the record can't be cheaply rewritten.
62d424f12e: Miners repeatedly scramble block data with a "nonce" (a number they keep changing) until the resulting fingerprint (a SHA-256 hash) starts with enough zeros. There's no shortcut: just guessing, millions of times.
76d7a339ef: Hard to find, instant to verify. Change a single letter and the fingerprint changes completely. That's why history can't be quietly edited.
d885d92e83: Press start. Your browser will guess until it finds a valid hash.
2154da3c81: Simplified: real Bitcoin double-hashes an 80-byte block header, and the network as a whole makes about a sextillion guesses per second.
c49fbb06d9: The first digital thing that can't be copied.
841d6da0ba: Photos, songs, files: anything digital can be copied for free, endlessly. That's why digital money always needed a bank in the middle, to stop you spending the same dollar twice.
83f0fd230c: Bitcoin solved this "double-spend problem" without any middleman. That's the invention. What email did for letters, bitcoin does for value: it moves across the planet in minutes, at any hour, with nobody's approval.
